A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures and supporting material are readable. v3 integrates material from v2's Appendices A and B into an expanded main text, allowing reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 explicitly describes the work as purely theoretical. Its main text and appendices report constructions, complexity proofs and mathematical illustrations, without original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 likewise reports theoretical algorithms, reductions and proofs without experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes. Its new Table 1 summarizes complexity classifications.

M1.justification: The reduction constructions change substantially. v3 replaces v2's homogenization-and-scaling construction for Lipschitz hardness with h(x,y)=f(x+Ty1) in Theorem 7.3, generalizes homogenization to deeper networks, and introduces Boolean-formula simulation and digit-extraction networks in Theorems 5.4 and 9.1. These change the constructed networks and computational procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or test scenarios for training or evaluation. The expanded coverage concerns formal decision problems and network classes.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods. DeepZ, DeepPoly, ZonoDual and other verification methods appear as related-work citations.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, preprocessing, training budgets, sample sizes or testing protocols. Changes to network dimensions and depth concern theoretical constructions.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness experiments, error analyses or empirical case studies. The function plots illustrate mathematical constructions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The randomized approximation statements concern theoretical success guarantees.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical measurements, performance rankings or experimental result entries. The added table and plots present theoretical classifications and constructed functions; changed mathematical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v3 adds W[P] membership results, depth-dependent W-hierarchy hardness, injectivity and other decision-problem results, and constant-dimension and joint-parameter lower bounds, including Corollary 9.4. Lemma 7.2 and Theorem 7.3 replace v2's flawed unit-ball argument in Appendix B.7 with regional-gradient reasoning and a new hardness reduction. Homogenization is generalized, norm-oracle assumptions become explicit, and the p=0 approximation claim is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions expand from W[1]-hardness for two- and three-layer networks to hardness at increasing levels of the W-hierarchy for arbitrary fixed depths. v3 additionally claims hardness parameterized by depth in constant dimension, resolves a deep-network injectivity question, and strengthens the claimed optimality of enumeration with respect to depth and dimension jointly.

C2.justification: v3 develops a substantive interpretation connecting network depth to the W-hierarchy and discusses possible computational depth separation. Its conclusion replaces several earlier open questions with W-/Th-hierarchy membership questions and qualifies the sparse, small-weight discussion to two-layer constructions. v2's explicit worst-case limitations paragraph disappears, although practical applicability caveats remain in the conclusion.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 in v3 documents region representations, sign-pattern enumeration, matrix updates and dimensionality tests for the enumeration approach previously sketched in v2's Appendices A.1 and B.2. This provides additional implementation-oriented detail for an existing algorithmic approach.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around Boolean circuits, interpretability, ICNN expressivity and threshold-circuit complexity. Section 8 cites Cao et al., Dewasurendra and Jayawardhana, and Das et al. (2026) as resolving the norm-maximization questions left open in v2, including deterministic approximation. This changes the research frontier against which the contribution is presented.

P1.justification: v3 integrates v2's appendix preliminaries and proofs into the main argument, creates a separate algorithmic-upper-bounds section, and reorganizes the Lipschitz and ICNN discussion. The abstract, contributions, proof explanations and concluding research agenda are extensively rewritten around depth as well as dimension.

P2.justification: v3 adds the complexity overview Table 1, an algorithm display, and new Figures 5, 6, 7 and 9. It expands v2's zonotope illustration into the network-to-zonotope diagram in Figure 8 and moves appendix Figure 5 to main-text Figure 3. The document also adopts a different article layout throughout.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs an important weakness in a core contribution: v2's Lipschitz-hardness proof relied on an invalid identification with maximum function magnitude on the unit ball, while v3 supplies regional-gradient reasoning and an explicit separating construction. The new membership and depth-sensitive hardness proofs substantially sharpen the complexity classification. Integrated proofs and Table 1 improve verifiability. These gains outweigh the loss of the explicit worst-case limitations paragraph.
